prompt_text: I need an AI marketing agency in Los Angeles. Which specific agencies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best AI marketing agency in Los Angeles?
answer_verbatim:
Good — I can give you a short, practical shortlist of LA-area agencies to call and why each one makes sense depending on your specific AI-marketing needs (creative, performance, personalization, analytics/ML, or product integration). If you want, tell me your budget and objectives and I’ll tighten the list to the best matches.

Recommended agencies to call (what they’re good at and why):

- R/GA (Los Angeles)
  - Why call: Big network creative + technology practice; strong at AI-driven creative systems, personalization at scale, and cross-channel product experiences.
  - Ask about: examples of AI-powered creative or product work, data integrations, and measurement frameworks.

- AKQA (Los Angeles)
  - Why call: Experience design and digital product focus with machine-learning and personalization capabilities — good for brand-led experiences that need smart automation.
  - Ask about: case studies mixing UX design and ML, timeline for prototyping, and team makeup (data scientists vs. creative technologists).

- Huge (Los Angeles)
  - Why call: User experience and commerce-focused agency that applies data and AI to conversion and CX improvements — strong for DTC/e‑commerce and product experiences.
  - Ask about: AI-driven personalization for e‑commerce, A/B testing approach, and sample KPIs they improved.

- Wpromote (El Segundo / LA)
  - Why call: Performance marketing shop known for programmatic, paid search/social, and AI/automation for campaign optimization — good if your priority is performance/ad ROI.
  - Ask about: AI tools they use for bidding/creative optimization and examples of improved CAC/ROAS.

- Tinuiti (LA presence)
  - Why call: Performance-first agency with strengths in paid media, Amazon, and data-driven creative optimization using AI tools — good for retail and multi-channel paid strategies.
  - Ask about: Amazon/marketplace AI strategies, creative testing cadence, and cross-channel measurement.

- Merkle (LA)
  - Why call: Data-driven CRM, customer-data-platform (CDP), and personalization at scale — ideal if you need AI applied to segmentation, lifecycle marketing, and identity resolution.
  - Ask about: CDP integrations, ML models for lifetime value/predictive churn, and compliance/data governance.

- Bounteous (LA)
  - Why call: Digital transformation, analytics, and experimentation with strong technical execution — good for teams who want to implement ML pipelines, analytics, or product integrations.
  - Ask about: implementation examples of AI models into customer-facing products and post-launch monitoring processes.

- VaynerMedia (LA office)
  - Why call: Social-first creative and creator-economy expertise combined with an appetite for rapid experimentation with new tech (including generative AI) — good for social campaigns that leverage AI-generated assets and scale creators.
  - Ask about: use of generative AI in social content, influencer-creative collaboration, and speed-to-market.

- Epsilon (LA / part of Publicis)
  - Why call: Strong in data-driven personalization and programmatic with proprietary tech stacks — good for large-scale CRM and precision targeting using AI.
  - Ask about: identity resolution, personalization engines, and sample uplift metrics.

How to prioritize who to call first
- If your goal is brand/creative innovation: start with R/GA, AKQA, VaynerMedia.
- If your goal is direct response / ROAS: start with Wpromote, Tinuiti.
- If your goal is customer-data, personalization, or ML pipelines: start with Merkle, Epsilon, Bounteous.

What to have ready before calls
- Short brief (1 page): your objective, target audience, primary channels, current monthly ad/spend baseline (if any), and timeline.
- Key success metrics (e.g., CAC, LTV, revenue, engagement).
- A few examples of competitors or campaigns you like.

What to ask on the first call (quick checklist)
- Have you done this before? (Ask for 1–2 relevant case studies and references.)
- Which AI tools/tech do you use vs. build in-house?
- Typical timeline and milestones for a pilot vs. full rollout.
- Team composition and points of contact (data scientist, product engineer, creative director).
- Pricing model (retainer, project, performance-based).
- Measurement and reporting cadence.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to 3 best-fit agencies if you tell me budget, industry, and primary goal.
- Draft a 1-page brief you can send prior to calls.
- Provide phone/website links and template email/LinkedIn outreach messages for each agency.

Which do you want me to do next?
